items.title: EU and US agree to accelerate steel tariff talks

featured_image.name: Tariffs, Šefčovič in Washington to close deal. EU aims at a 10 per cent  "flat" tariff

items.description:
EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have agreed to speed up negotiations over transatlantic steel and aluminum trade, following high-level meetings in Washington this week aimed at breaking a long-standing deadlock over 50% US tariffs on European metals.[1][2]

Šefčovič proposed that both sides return to the concept of "ringfencing" their steel sectors and trading on "very favorable terms," according to statements relayed through financial news wires on Thursday. The meetings, held April 22-24, marked Šefčovič's first visit to Washington since the EU-US trade agreement was concluded in July 2025.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: US sanctions major Chinese refinery, 40 shippers over Iran oil

featured_image.name: Here's How Much Scott Bessent Is Worth

items.description:
The Trump administration on Friday imposed sanctions on Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co., Ltd., one of China's largest independent oil refineries, along with approximately 40 shipping companies and tankers for their role in transporting Iranian oil, the Treasury Department announced.[1]

The action, carried out under the administration's "Economic Fury" campaign, represents the latest escalation in Washington's effort to sever Iran's primary revenue source — its oil exports — amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict that has disrupted global energy markets since February.

items.title: Witkoff and Kushner to head to Pakistan for new Iran talks

featured_image.name: Witkoff and Kushner expected to meet Iranian foreign minister in Pakistan

items.description: The White House confirmed on Friday that U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Pakistan for a fresh round of negotiations with Iranian officials, as Washington and Tehran attempt to break a diplomatic stalemate that has persisted since their first face-to-face talks collapsed nearly two weeks ago.

items.title: Netanyahu reveals secret prostate cancer diagnosis and treatment

featured_image.name: Netanyahu to undergo prostate surgery - JNS.org

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed on Friday that he was diagnosed with prostate cancer and quietly underwent radiation therapy, marking the first time the longest-serving leader in Israel's history has acknowledged a cancer diagnosis. In a statement posted on X, the 76-year-old said he is now cancer-free and in "excellent physical condition."[1][2]

items.title: China moves to block US investment in top AI startups

featured_image.name: Chinese AI startups make gains in challenge to US-based OpenAI

items.description: The United States and China took dueling steps this week to tighten controls on each other's access to artificial intelligence technology and capital, widening a tech rivalry that has become a defining feature of the bilateral relationship.

items.title: Iran claims seized cargo ship was carrying dialysis supplies, demands release

featured_image.name: Watch as U.S. Marines Seize the Iranian Vessel 'Touska' in Gulf of ...

items.description:
Iran's mission to the United Nations on Thursday condemned the American seizure of the Iranian-flagged cargo vessel Touska, claiming the ship was carrying critical dialysis supplies and medical equipment when it was intercepted on April 19 in the Sea of Oman. The statement, posted on the social platform X, described the action as "a flagrant breach of international law" and demanded accountability and the immediate release of the vessel and its crew.[1][2][3]

The Iranian Red Crescent Society backed Tehran's account, stating in a separate announcement that part of the Touska's cargo consisted of raw materials needed to produce consumable medical supplies for kidney dialysis patients. The supplies belonged to Saha Medical Equipment Company, a subsidiary of the Red Crescent, according to the organization. "Any disruption in the supply of these critical items could directly threaten the health and lives of patients in need of dialysis services," the Red Crescent warned.[4]

items.title: China picks 5 global partners for Mars sample-return mission

featured_image.name: China's Tianwen-3 to bring rocks and soil from Mars by 2031, puts ...

items.description:
The China National Space Administration on Friday revealed the five international collaboration projects selected for its Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission, marking a concrete step toward what could become humanity's first retrieval of material from the red planet.

The announcement came during the opening ceremony of the 11th Space Day of China in Chengdu, Sichuan Province. CNSA said it received 28 proposals after issuing a call for cooperation in April 2025 that offered 20 kilograms of payload capacity to international partners. The five winning projects were chosen based on scientific value, mission support, engineering feasibility, and technological maturity.[1][2]

items.title: Study: 36% of land animal habitats face compounding climate extremes by 2085

featured_image.name: Multiple extreme weather events to impact 36% land animal habitats ...

items.description: More than a third of all land animal habitats could be exposed to multiple types of climate-driven extreme events — heatwaves, wildfires, droughts and floods — by 2085 if greenhouse gas emissions are not rapidly reduced, according to a study published Thursday in Nature Ecology & Evolution.[1][2]

items.title: Hegseth says US naval blockade on Iran is 'going global'

featured_image.name: Pentagon chief Hegseth says US blockade on Iran 'going global ...

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade on Iran is expanding beyond the Middle East, warning that no vessel can transit the Strait of Hormuz without American approval.

"Our blockade is growing and going global," Hegseth told reporters at the Pentagon, according to Reuters. "No one sails from the Strait of Hormuz to anywhere in the world without the permission of the United States Navy."[1][2][3]

Hegseth, appearing alongside Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Air Force General Dan Caine, said 34 ships had been turned around from the Strait of Hormuz since the blockade began on April 13. He added that Tehran still has a chance to make a "good deal" with Washington.[2][4]

items.title: Macron rejects US approach to Iran at EU summit

featured_image.name: France's Macron says Iran responsible for destabilising region ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron called for a swift return to stability in the Middle East and publicly rejected Washington's approach toward Iran, declaring that negotiations must be "systematic" and rooted in diplomacy rather than military pressure or economic coercion. Speaking on Thursday at the informal EU summit in Ayia Napa, Cyprus, Macron warned that the spillover from the US-Israel war on Iran is unsettling the global economy.[1][2]

"It is in everyone's interest for stability to return as soon as possible and for the world's economies to be reassured," Macron said, according to Al Jazeera. He added: "Dialogue with Iran must be carried out in a systematic manner, not through targeted blockades or similar measures".[2]

items.title: Trump orders military to 'shoot and kill' Iranian boats in Hormuz standoff

featured_image.name: US military threatens to blockade all Iranian ports starting on Monday

items.description: The standoff between the United States and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz showed no signs of easing on Thursday, with President Donald Trump declaring "total control" of the critical waterway and ordering the military to "shoot and kill" Iranian small boats laying mines in the passage. The escalating confrontation has pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel and brought global energy trade through the strait — responsible for roughly 20% of the world's oil shipments — to a near halt.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Oil nears $110 in fifth straight rally as Hormuz standoff intensifies

featured_image.name: Oil prices surge amid mixed signals on US-Iran peace talks

items.description:
Crude oil prices climbed for a fifth straight session on Friday, with both major benchmarks rising over 1 percent as the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively shut to commercial traffic and diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran showed little sign of progress.

Brent crude futures rose 1.17 percent while West Texas Intermediate gained 1.12 percent in early Asian trading, according to the Economic Times. The move extends a rally that accelerated on Thursday, when Brent surged over 3 percent to close above $105 per barrel.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil tops $106 as stalled Iran talks drag Asian markets lower

featured_image.name: The U.S. military says it will blockade Iranian ports as Iran peace ...

items.description: Markets across Asia declined on Friday as oil prices climbed and stalled U.S.-Iran peace negotiations kept investors on edge. The losses followed a pullback on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 fell 0.4% on Thursday, halting a weekslong rally that had carried it to all-time highs.[1][2]

items.title: Scientists discover seismic 'stopping phase' in earthquakes

featured_image.name: Japan: KyotoU PEGS away at catching quakes at light speed ...

items.description: Researchers at Kyoto University have discovered a previously unrecognized seismic signal — a distinct "stopping phase" — that marks the moment large earthquakes cease rupturing along a fault. The finding, published Wednesday in the journal Science, could reshape how engineers and seismologists assess earthquake hazards near major fault lines.[1][2]

items.title: Oil surges past $100 as Trump orders Navy to fire on Iranian boats

featured_image.name: US to ‘shoot and kill’ Iranian boats laying mines in Hormuz, Trump says

items.description:
Oil prices surged past $100 a barrel on Thursday as President Donald Trump ordered the U.S. Navy to "shoot and kill" any Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, deepening a standoff that has disrupted one of the world's most critical shipping lanes for nearly two months.[1][2][3]

Brent crude climbed more than 3% during the session, while West Texas Intermediate also rose sharply, as investors weighed the prospect of prolonged supply disruptions in the Persian Gulf. Asian and European stock markets pulled back from recent highs, with MSCI's global equity index retreating from a record peak.[4][5]

items.title: House panel advances bill cutting US UN funding by 78%

featured_image.name: Trump's FY2027 Budget Is Not Just a Spending Plan - ONEST Network

items.description:
The House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs advanced a fiscal year 2027 spending bill on Wednesday that would dramatically reduce US funding for international organizations, slashing contributions by roughly 78% and effectively zeroing out US dues for the UN regular budget.

The bill, released on April 22 and marked up on April 23, allocates $310.2 million for Contributions to International Organizations — down from $1.39 billion enacted in fiscal year 2026. It provides $489.5 million for UN peacekeeping activities, a roughly 60% reduction from the $1.23 billion provided in the current fiscal year. The legislation eliminates the International Organizations and Programs account entirely, cutting all voluntary US contributions to agencies including UNICEF, the UN Development Programme, and UN Women.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump threatens UK with tariffs over digital services tax

featured_image.name: Trump warns of 'big tariff' if UK does not drop digital services ...

items.description: President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that the United States could impose a "big tariff" on the United Kingdom if it does not eliminate its digital services tax on American tech companies, escalating a long-running dispute over levies that Washington considers discriminatory against US firms.

items.title: INNIO completes first 3 MW hydrogen backup test for data centers

featured_image.name: Hydrogen moves INNIO's Jenbacher site closer to climate neutrality ...

items.description: INNIO Group and the Net Zero Innovation Hub for Data Centers have completed what they describe as the world's first demonstration of 100% hydrogen-fueled backup power at the 3 MW scale, a milestone aimed at replacing diesel generators in mission-critical data center operations. The test, announced on Wednesday, was witnessed by technical experts from Microsoft, Google, and Data4.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended three weeks

featured_image.name: Trump's Lebanon ceasefire takes Israel by surprise

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has been extended by three weeks, according to a post on Truth Social, just days before the truce was set to expire on April 26. The extension came as Israeli and Lebanese diplomats held a second round of rare direct talks in Washington.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Nuclear power surges worldwide as Chernobyl's 40th anniversary approaches

featured_image.name: 2026 China International Nuclear Industry Exhibition

items.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, nuclear energy is experiencing a resurgence that would have seemed unthinkable in the decades following the catastrophic 1986 explosion. More than 400 nuclear reactors now operate across 31 countries, with roughly 70 more under construction, and a growing coalition of nations has pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050.[1][2]
